page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-96-standardlssd is an x86_64 server configuration belonging to the storage-optimized instance family. It is equipped with 96 dedicated virtual CPUs and 756.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature graphical processing units or hardware accelerators, directing all available compute and bus resources toward central processing and memory-intensive execution.

Storage capability is defined by a dense local subsystem totaling 22,549 GB of NVMe SSD capacity across six local drives. This integrated local drive structure delivers direct bus-attached storage, avoiding the latency and throughput constraints associated with network-attached block devices. Network configuration provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The dense co-location of 96 dedicated cores, 756 GB of RAM, and over 22 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage creates an efficient operational footprint for read- and write-heavy workloads. It mitigates the recurring overhead of configuring separate external high-IOPS disk volumes. This architecture is suitable for distributed NoSQL databases, large-scale transactional databases, real-time analytics pipelines, and search indexing platforms.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-96-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for data-intensive enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 756.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per core. A key characteristic of the instance is its integrated storage subsystem, consisting of 22,549 GB of local NVMe SSD storage allocated across six local solid-state drives. The configuration contains zero GPUs and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With high memory density coupled to extensive local NVMe capacity, the resource profile eliminates external storage latency bottlenecks. This setup is particularly effective for large distributed databases, high-throughput transactional systems, in-memory caching platforms with disk persistence, and big data search indexes that require rapid concurrent I/O throughput.
